 ORDER
This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.154/2022, registered at P.S.-Mahila Thana, District-Rewa (M.P.) for commission of offence under Section 376(2)(N), 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act with Section 67(A) and 66(E) of Information Technology Act.
He is in detention since 6.7.2022.

A s per the prosecution story, on 9.4.2022 minor prosecutrix lodged a complaint in writing before Police Station Govindgarh, District Rewa alleging that in 2021 she was student of Class 12th and was studying in school.
Sister of accused was her classmate.

Her classmate's brother occasionally used to Lalesh Nirala @ Goldy @ Raj Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188646682/

sentences.text: It was further alleged that almost one year ago sometime in March 2021 when she had gone to her class mate's house, classmate's brother/ accused gave her some intoxicated drink and thereafter took off her cloth, raped her and filmed obscene video.
Thereafter, extending threat of making the video viral, he repeatedly committed rape/ aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.

But when she refused to bow down before his illegal demands,
he shared the obscene video with some of the villagers.
FIR was registered.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
In this case FIR has been lodged almost after one year of the incident.
Prosecutrix is not appearing before the trial Court for tendering her evidence.
In the aforesaid pretext, it has been prayed that applicant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the State has opposed grant of bail to the applicant.

It is a case where the applicant/accused has not only raped/ made aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the minor prosecutrix but also filmed her obscene video with himself and thereafter by extending threat of making videos viral, exploited her for a number of time.
The incident came into light only when the applicant/ accused made the video viral.

Having taken into consideration the facts of the case and material available on record including gravity of offence and quantum of sentence for such offence, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.
Therefore, this first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant- Lalesh Nirala @ Goldy @ Raj Saket is dismissed.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Lalesh Nirala @ Goldy @ Raj Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023
